issues.legal_issue: Entitlement to a ryotwari patta for an iruvaram service inam depends on whether the original grant was made to the religious institution or to the individual service-holder.
material_facts: The inam comprised both the melvaram and kudivaram, and the original title deed was unavailable.
Historical records, including a sanad, a title deed, administrative documents and earlier court proceedings, supported the conclusion that the religious institution was the original grantee.
The inam register described the grant as religious and permanent; those entries, considered with the other records, also supported an institutional grant.
The service-holders possessed and enjoyed the land while performing service for the institution.
issues.conclusion: The original grant was to the religious institution, which was entitled to the ryotwari patta. The service-holders held possession derivatively in connection with their service and could not claim individual title to the land.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 2(5) of the Madras Minor Inams (Abolition and Conversion into Ryotwari) Act, 1963, an inam may be a grant of the melvaram alone or of both the melvaram and kudivaram, confirmed or recognised by the Government. Under Section 8(2)(ii), for an iruvaram minor inam granted for the support of a religious institution or for connected service, the institution or the individual rendering service is entitled to the patta, depending on the original grant. The grant’s nature is determined from the evidence as a whole; possession and enjoyment by service-holders do not establish an individual grant where the evidence shows they held derivatively. Buddu Satyanarayana v. Konduru Venkatapayya supports treating the deity as grantee where the evidence identifies the temple as the original grantee. Poohari Fakir Sadavarthy of Bondilipuram v. Commissioner, Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments cautions against accepting particular inam-register entries at face value without considering other recorded matters. T.V.V. Narasimham v. State of Orissa is cited for the principle that later proceedings do not change the character of a right confirmed on the original grantee.

predicates.minor_inam_pattta_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal concerning entitlement to a land-settlement patta for a minor inam.
predicates.iruvaram_service_grant: The inam is a service grant comprising both the superior and occupancy interests in the land.
predicates.institutional_grant_indicated_by_corrobo: Historical, administrative or judicial records, considered together, indicate that the religious institution received the original grant.
predicates.service_holders_possess_in_connection_wi: The service-holders possess or enjoy the land in connection with services they perform for the religious institution.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerns a service grant comprising both interests in the land, the records indicate an original institutional grant, and service-holders possess in connection with their service, the religious institution is entitled to the patta.

issues.legal_issue: Entries in an inam register are significant evidence of the nature of an inam grant but are not conclusive when considered in isolation.
material_facts: The inam register described the grant as religious and permanent.
Other records, including historical grant documents, a title deed, administrative documents and earlier court proceedings, bore on who received the original grant.
The original title deed was unavailable, so the register entries had to be assessed alongside the other evidence.
issues.conclusion: The inam-register entries had to be given due weight but could not alone determine the nature of the grant; they had to be read with the other evidence.
issues.legal_principle: The entries in an Inam Fair Register are acts of the State and may have great evidentiary value, particularly when considered with survey and settlement records. They are not conclusive merely because they describe an inam as religious or permanent; the entries must be read with the other evidence and with due regard to the context of the recorded information. Vatticherukuru Village Panchayat v. Nori Venkatarama Deekshitulu and Jammi Raja Rao v. Sri Anjaneyaswami Temple support the importance of inam-register entries. Arunachellam Chetty v. Venkatachalapathi Guruswamigal explains the evidentiary significance of the register, while Poohari Fakir Sadavarthy of Bondilipuram v. Commissioner, Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments establishes that entries in particular columns cannot be accepted at face value without considering other recorded matters.
